text_blocks.snippet: Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome (WHS) is a genetic disorder caused by a deletion of genetic material from the short arm (p arm) of chromosome 4. This deletion, often referred to as "4p-" or "4p deletion," results in a range of developmental and physical abnormalities, though the severity varies greatly.
snippet_highlighted_words: a genetic disorder caused by a deletion of genetic material from the short arm (p arm) of chromosome 4

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: A deletion of a portion of the short arm of chromosome 4 (4p).

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Can include intellectual disability, developmental delays, seizures, distinctive facial features (wide-set eyes, prominent forehead, small chin), growth delays, heart defects, and other physical anomalies.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Typically involves clinical findings and genetic testing to confirm the deletion of the 4p region.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: There is no cure, and treatment focuses on managing symptoms and providing supportive care. This may include therapies for development, surgery for physical abnormalities, and medications for seizures.
